title: GLM-5.2
hook: z.ai's GLM-5.2 became the strongest open-weights model of mid-2026 — the first reported to clear 80% on Terminal-Bench and a coding favorite that rivals top closed models at a fraction of the cost.
key_points: Open-weights model from z.ai (formerly Zhipu AI), released mid-June 2026 — successor to GLM-4.6.
Reported by Cline as the first open-weights model to cross 80% on Terminal-Bench, an agentic terminal-coding benchmark.
Topped the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index among open-weights models and ranked #1 on Design Arena.
Drew unusual praise for coding strength — frontier-level results at far lower cost than leading closed models.
content_html: GLM-5.2, from Beijing-based z.ai (formerly Zhipu AI), landed in mid-June 2026 as the successor to GLM-4.6 — and quickly became the open-weights model everyone was talking about. According to the coding tool Cline, it was the first open-weights model to cross 80% on Terminal-Bench, a benchmark for agentic terminal and coding tasks, and it climbed to the top of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index among open models.
extra_html:
What's new

Community benchmarks placed GLM-5.2 at the front of the open-weights pack: #1 on Design Arena, leader on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index for open models, and — in its "max" configuration — among the top three models tested across both open and proprietary systems. The loudest praise was for coding, where developers (including Vercel's CEO) reported being "almost shocked" by its quality.

Why it matters

GLM-5.2 continues the run of strong open-weights Chinese models — alongside DeepSeek, Qwen, and Kimi — that have been steadily closing the gap with closed frontier labs. The headline is cost and control: a self-hostable model approaching the best closed systems on coding, at a fraction of the price. As one popular post put it, "open weights is back." Benchmark claims here come from the community and tool vendors rather than a formal paper, so treat exact rankings as directional.

related.title: GLM-4.6
related.hook: Zhipu's GLM-4.6 is an open-weight MoE that became a popular drop-in coding backend — near Claude Sonnet 4 on real-world coding, with a 200K context and a permissive license.

related.title: DeepSeek-V4: Sparse Attention, Million-Token Default
related.hook: DeepSeek-V4 makes a 1M-token context window the default and pairs token-wise compression with sparse attention, so long-context inference no longer pays the usual compute and memory tax.

related.title: Kimi K2: Open Agentic Intelligence
related.hook: Moonshot's Kimi K2 is a trillion-parameter open-weight Mixture-of-Experts model built agentic-first — and trained at that scale without a single loss spike using the MuonClip optimizer.
